# gatekeep-pr #82: deliver-nits checkpoint, then terminal fix-nits checkpoint

## Checkpoint A: course `deliver-nits`, record `/tmp/gatekeep-82.record`

### 1. Record pick and validate the record

The pick is the bare numeric `deliver with nits` row. It maps to course `deliver-nits`.

I validate `/tmp/gatekeep-82.record` against `consent.target`:
- base repository `orchard/widgets`
- PR `82`
- base `main`

I persist the course and accounting before any course-authorized write.

`gauntlet_setting({ key: "closureReview" })` returns `maxFixRounds 5`. I write these values to `/tmp/gatekeep-82.record`:
- `course: deliver-nits`
- `repair.rounds_cap: 10`
- `repair.syncs_cap: 10`
- `repair.rounds_used: 0`
- `repair.syncs_used: 0`
- `repair.poll_deadline: null`

**Tracker:** I init no new stages; the plan tracker is already open from the first run. `gather, provision, verify, review, report, menu` are closed. There is no `sync` stage because `--rebase` was not passed. Step 7 re-opens only the stage it re-enters, and none is re-entered yet.

### 2. Next-action boundary read (read-only)

I run `gh pr view 82 --json headRefOid,state,body,baseRefName,mergeable,mergeStateStatus`. The results:
- head `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`
- state `OPEN`
- base `main`, which matches `consent.target`
- body unchanged

No head move, body change or target change occurred.

### 3. D3 step 1: Exit check

- **Readiness:** fails. Blockers P1/L2, P2 and P3 are open.
- **Obstacle and cap:** none match.
- **Course:** delivery continues.

### 4. Wave setup (`fix-wave.md`)

- **pre_wave_head:** I record `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
- **Local conflict check:**
  - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-82 fetch origin main`
  - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-82 merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD`
  - Exit 0 means the head is conflict-free. Together with no CONFLICTING or BEHIND state, there is no sync trigger. `syncs_used` stays 0.
- **Settings:**
  - `gauntlet_setting({ key: "loopEngine" })` returns `maxIterationsPerRow 6` and `escalateAfter 2`.
  - `gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" })` resolves `implModel`.
- **Merge base:** `git -C /work/widgets-pr-82 merge-base origin/main aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` returns `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`.
- **Scoped runners:** I read `git show bbbb...:AGENTS.md`, which labels two scoped runners:
  - `cd core && node --test <files>`
  - `cd cli && node --test <files>`

  Each path is made relative to its runner's directory and inserted bare, because every character is in `[A-Za-z0-9/._-]`. `npm test` is never used as a scoped command.

### 5. Finding artifacts

Both files are written beside the record, outside the checkout, and never staged. I write the derived spec first, then the ledger.

### 7. Handling of P3 and C1

**P3 is a description target, not an AC or ledger row.** It goes through `### Description repair` in the orchestrator. No worker, commit, round charge or test run is involved.

At write time, which comes later and before the mixed wave's single head-changing push:
1. Re-fetch head and body, and compare both with the proposal's `assessed_head` and `original_body`.
2. On a match, run `gh pr edit 82 -R orchard/widgets --body-file <temp>`, preserving unrelated body text.
3. Read back the body and head.
4. Dispatch a fresh `worker` in Section B `description recheck` mode.
5. Close only P3's claim contribution, and only on that helper's `resolved` closure line.

The claim stays in `affected_claims` for the narrow recheck before readiness. Nothing is written yet, because this is an external write and the exercise stops before it.

**C1 stays an unposted drafted reply.** Course authority never covers replies. C1 needs its own explicit `reply 1` pick and remains in the ledger with its triage label.

### 8. Stop point

The next step would be:
- write `iterations: 1`
- write `pending: 1 | gatekeep | aaaa...`
- dispatch `loop-implementer` for `target: 1`, with:
  - `cwd /work/widgets-pr-82`, `context: "fresh"`, `async: false`
  - the shared worker context with `HEAD_BEFORE` = `aaaa...`
  - `Rules: AGENTS.md`
  - `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: cd core && node --test test/retry.test.mjs`
  - no `model` (attempts 0 is below threshold `min(2, 5) = 2`)

**I stop here, before that write and dispatch.**

- **Assessed SHA:** verification and the brief assessed `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.
- **Sync line:** none renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.
- **Verdict and menu:** neither renders. Under deliver-nits, no menu appears before an exit, and this checkpoint is not an exit.

## Deliver with nits checkpoint

### 1. Resolve budgets and prepare the wave

```text
gauntlet_setting({ key: "closureReview" })
gauntlet_setting({ key: "loopEngine" })
gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" })
```

These resolve `maxFixRounds: 5`, row allowance `6`, escalation threshold `2`, and an available escalation model. I initialize missing wave caps to 10 rounds and 10 syncs without resetting existing usage.

I run, in order:

```bash
git -C /work/widgets-pr-82 status --porcelain
git -C /work/widgets-pr-82 rev-parse HEAD
git -C /work/widgets-pr-82 merge-base origin/main aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
git -C /work/widgets-pr-82 show bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb:AGENTS.md
```

The tree is clean, HEAD is the assessed head, and the merge-base is `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. I use the supplied merge-base configuration and scoped runners, not configuration from the PR head.

I retain the stored scope baseline and check the existing helper/no-progress checkpoint before further work. No retained obstacle prevents preparation.

I persist the wave's `pre_wave_head` and `round_start_head` as the assessed head, `counted: false`, and `stage: apply`. I do not increment rounds or syncs.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact that Before kept was lost in After; the only movement is upward. Before explicitly declined to write any derived spec or companion ledger ("gatekeep-pr has neither artifact"), split N1 and N2 into separate wave rows, and treated the record's repair.wave plus evidence packs as the ledger stand-in, so n1, n2, n3, n4, n5 and n7 all failed there. After renders both sibling artifacts beside the OS-temp record for each checkpoint, merges P1/L2 into row 1, batches both nits into a single last row carrying the union of the two prefixed scoped commands (with npm test confined to the ledger's verification line and commands kept in the row task rather than a column), persists the spec/ledger paths in repair.wave, keeps the authoritative doc/specs/retry-budget.md scope contract in the Scope block, routes P3 through description repair with the head/body compare-and-swap and claim recheck, leaves C1 as an unposted draft awaiting a reply pick, and stops before the iterations/pending write and loop-implementer dispatch in both checkpoints. The Change itself (rendering open prior-review items under Blockers/Nits with the reviewer's posted text and locator unchanged) has no prior-review items to exercise in this case, so it cannot be observed here; the wording to keep is the explicit "written beside the record, outside the checkout, never staged" and "carried in the row task, not in a ledger column" sentences, and the single fix-nits batch AC line, since those are what carry n4 and n5. If you later add prior-item rendering text, keep it out of the AC/ledger-row admission narration so it does not read as minting rows for prior items.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Nothing regressed: After keeps every fact Before kept (P3/C1 non-file routing and the no-dispatch stop) and additionally satisfies n1–n5 and n7, which Before failed outright because it declared that no derived spec or companion ledger exists and refused to write them, split nits into separate per-item command rows, and never produced the terminal checkpoint's single-row ledger. After writes the spec and ledger as OS-temp siblings of each record, carries the PR title/body/original intent and the assessed-head spec path in Scope, builds exactly three rows (P1+L2 combined, P2, one N1+N2 batch) and one terminal row, persists repair.wave.spec/ledger, and gives the nit row the prefixed command union while leaving npm test as the ledger verification line only. The prior-item rendering clarification did not touch any of these facts, as intended; to keep this stable, keep the spec/ledger emission wording separate from the prior-item rendering contract so the Blockers/Nits verbatim-text rule is never read as suppressing finding-artifact creation.
